paragraphs: The Manitowoc Company, Inc. ("Manitowoc" or the "Company") was founded in 1902, and is headquartered in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, United States. Manitowoc, through its wholly-owned subsidiaries, provides high quality, customer-focused lifting products and services world-wide through its Grove, Manitowoc, National Crane, Potain, Shuttlelift, and Upfits by Aspen Equipment brands and its support-focused subsidiary MGX Equipment Services. For more information, visit www.manitowoc.com. The information on our website is not part of this or any other report we file with or furnish to the SEC and is not incorporated herein by reference.

The Company has three reportable segments; the Americas segment, the Europe and Africa ("EURAF") segment, and the Middle East and Asia Pacific ("MEAP") segment. The Americas reporting segment includes the North America and South America continents. The EURAF reporting segment includes the Europe and Africa continents, excluding the Middle East region. The MEAP reporting segment includes the Asia and Australia continents and the Middle East region. The segments were identified using the "management approach," which designates the internal organization that is used by management for making operating decisions and assessing performance. Refer to Part II, Item 7. "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" and Note 17, "Segments," for additional information on our reporting segments.

Manitowoc's vision is that we build the physical communities and structures for current and future generations. Our Mission is integral to this vision; We aspire to deliver the highest level of customer confidence and trust in the lifting industry. Our Core Values are the guiding principles for our employees to ensure that we meet our Vision and Mission. These Core Values are:

(1) We succeed when our customers excel: We are committed to our customers' success, we provide a customer first experience every time, we are focused on improving the customer experience every day, and we provide reliable and excellent service.
(2) We do what is right: We work in a safe and environmentally responsible way, we respect others, we behave in an ethical way and we deliver quality work.
(3) We work as a team: We help each other to meet customer needs, we put the team first, we collaborate and support team members and we foster open, two-way communication.
(4) We deliver results: We do what we say we will do, we focus on continuous improvement and innovation, and we strive to exceed customer expectations.
(5) We act as a role model: We celebrate successes and learn from failures, we approach every day with a can-do-attitude, and we have fun.

Manitowoc is transforming from a product-focused company into a customer-centric business focused on providing a full suite of lifting services to grow our aftermarket presence. Alongside our continued commitment to developing innovative lifting products and a robust new product development pipeline, we are expanding our non-new machine sales through our CRANES+50 strategy. Non-new machine sales are less capital intensive, more profitable, and less cyclical. Our long-term goal is to generate sustainable returns to our stakeholders, positioning Manitowoc as a stronger and more resilient company.

We launched our CRANES+50 strategy in 2021 to specifically grow our non-new machine sales to transform the Company from a products-focused business into a customer-centric business providing a full suite of lifting services to grow our aftermarket presence. This transition is instrumental in supporting our long-term aspirations. The CRANES+50 strategy is far more than incremental aftermarket growth; it is also about delivering complete lifting solutions for our customers. This includes strengthening our service footprint by expanding our distribution reach, broadening our portfolio with new and complementary
products, providing more service offerings, and introducing digital solutions to provide excellent value-added support for our customers.
Notable initiatives include the following:

Americas: In 2021, we acquired the assets of two companies, Aspen Equipment Company ("Aspen") and the crane business of H&E Equipment Services, Inc. (now MGX Equipment Services, LLC, or "MGX Equipment Services"), which expanded our ability to provide new machine sales, used machine sales, aftermarket parts, remanufacturing, and service support to a variety of end market customers. In 2022, we completed the acquisition of certain assets of the crane rental fleet of Honnen Equipment Company ("Honnen"), which expanded our rental portfolio and direct-to-customer footprint in Colorado, Wyoming and Nebraska. Additionally, in 2023, we added key territories including Missouri and South Carolina and, in 2024, we relocated to larger locations in Louisiana and Arizona. In early 2025, we opened an expanded facility in Nashville, Tennessee and acquired certain territories and related assets of Ring Power Corporation, further expanding our direct-to-customer territories in Georgia, North Carolina, and South Carolina. The acquisition of the assets of these businesses and additional territories advanced our strategy to expand our aftermarket activities within North America. We currently offer 17 full-service branch locations in 15 states with over 175 field service technicians that provide industry-leading technical competencies and exceptional customer support. In early 2026, we announced a new distribution agreement with Hiab to offer loader cranes across 13 states, expanding the products we can sell to our customers and providing service for those products.

EURAF and MEAP: Since 2021, we have grown our European tower crane rental fleet original equipment cost by $27.3 million to enhance our support to customers. We continue to enhance the portfolio of aftermarket services performed in Europe, such as sale of parts and whole goods accessories, on-site repairs, technical support, erection and decommissioning services, crane remanufacturing, training services, and digital solutions. In 2025, we opened new and upgraded service locations in Meru, France; Bouaye, France; and Warsaw, Poland, enhancing our service coverage for customers. In Europe, we currently offer 17 service locations in eight countries with over 220 field service technicians. In addition, our Australia location has expanded the services and complementary products it sells based on the needs of our customers.

headings: Risks Relating to Our Business, Operations and Industry
Macroeconomic conditions and geopolitical events could have a material adverse impact on our business, financial condition, cash flows and results of operations.
Because we participate in end markets that are highly competitive, our net sales and profits could decline as we respond, or fail to effectively respond, to competition.
Unfair foreign competition could adversely affect our financial results.
We have significant manufacturing and sales of our products outside of the United States and such international operations could be subject to a number of risks specific to these countries.
If we do not develop new and innovative products or if customers in our markets do not accept them, our results could be negatively affected.
We depend on our key executive officers, managers and skilled personnel and may have difficulty retaining and recruiting qualified employees.
We may not be able to maintain our engineering, technological and manufacturing expertise.
Any disruption in our information systems could disrupt our operations and would be adverse to our business and financial operations.
If we fail to identify, manage, complete and appropriately integrate acquisitions, strategic alliances, joint ventures or other significant transactions, it could adversely affect our future results.
If we fail to maintain an effective network for distribution of our products and services, it could affect our business and financial results.
Increasing costs of doing business in many countries in which we operate may adversely affect our business and financial results.
Our operations and profitability could suffer if we experience problems with labor relations.
Our inability to recover from natural or man-made disasters or public health crises could adversely affect our business and financial results.
Financial Risks

Some of our customers may not be able to obtain financing with third parties to purchase our products, and we could incur expenses associated with our assistance to customers in securing third-party financing.
Our leverage could impair our operations and financial condition.
Our results of operations are subject to exchange rate and other currency risks. A significant movement in exchange rates could adversely impact our results of operations and cash flows.
Exposure to additional tax liabilities could have a negative impact on our operating results.

Our goodwill and intangible assets represent a significant amount of our total assets; as a result, impairment charges have had, and future impairment charges may have, an adverse effect on our results of operations.
We face risks associated with our pension and other postretirement benefit obligations.
Legal and Regulatory Risks
Environmental liabilities that may arise could be material.

Our international sales and operations are subject to applicable laws relating to trade, tariffs, export controls, and foreign corrupt practices, the violation of which could adversely affect our operations.

If we do not meet customers' product quality and reliability standards and expectations, we may experience increased or unexpected product warranty claims and other adverse consequences to our business.
Compliance or the failure to comply with regulations and governmental policies could cause us to incur significant expense.
If we fail to protect our intellectual property rights or maintain our rights to use licensed intellectual property, our business could be adversely affected.
paragraphs: The Company's financial position, results of operations, and cash flows are subject to various risks, many of which are not exclusively within the Company's control, which may cause actual performance to differ materially from historical or projected future performance. Investors should carefully consider information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K in light of the risk factors described below.

Macroeconomic conditions, including inflation, elevated interest rates, and tariffs, as well as prior supply chain, labor and logistics constraints, have had, and may continue to have, a negative impact on our ability to convert backlog into revenue (the timing of sales) which could, and has, impacted our financial condition, cash flows, and results of operations. In addition, prior shipping constraints resulted in delays in shipments in certain regions. Continuing or worsening macroeconomic conditions may have a material adverse impact on our financial condition, results of operations, and/or cash flows.

Geopolitical events, including the ongoing conflicts in Ukraine and in the Middle East, have led to and may continue to lead to logistic constraints, higher logistic costs, and significant volatility in raw material and component costs in Europe, exacerbating the inflation and tariff situation, which may have a material adverse impact on our financial condition, results of operations, and/or cash flows.

Our business is subject to risks related to, among other factors, tariffs and other trade protection measures put in place by the United States or other countries, as well as U.S.-international trade relations, including those with China and the European Union.

As of December 31, 2025, the U.S. has implemented country-specific trade agreements with key partners including the European Union, Japan, and the United Kingdom, featuring modified tariff structures and industry-specific exemptions. The

U.S. continues to negotiate trade agreements with other countries, including China, which currently have varying reciprocal tariffs. In addition, the U.S. government imposed 50% tariffs on new steel and aluminum derivative products which include certain of our crane components and models. These tariffs apply to imports from nearly all countries, with the United Kingdom subject to a reduced 25% rate.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes appearing in Part II, Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

Overview: The Manitowoc Company, Inc. ("Manitowoc" or the "Company") was founded in 1902, and is headquartered in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, United States. Manitowoc, through its wholly-owned subsidiaries, provides high quality, customer-focused lifting products and services world-wide through its Grove, Manitowoc, National Crane, Potain, Shuttlelift, and Upfits by Aspen Equipment brands and its support-focused subsidiary MGX Equipment Services. For more information, visit www.manitowoc.com. The information on our website is not part of this or any other report we file with or furnish to the SEC and is not incorporated herein by reference.
All dollar amounts are in millions throughout the tables included in Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations unless otherwise indicated.

Orders and backlog are not measures defined by accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America ("GAAP") and our methodology for determining orders and backlog may vary from the methodology used by other companies. Management uses orders and backlog for capacity and resource planning. The Company believes this information is useful to investors to provide an indication of future revenues. Backlog represents the dollar value of orders which are expected to be recognized in net sales in the future. Orders are included in backlog when an executed binding contract with a price that has a floor has been received but has not been recognized in net sales.

Orders for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased 22.7% to $2,359.0 million from $1,922.8 million for the same period in 2024. The increase in orders was primarily due to higher demand in the Americas and EURAF segments. This was partially offset by lower demand in the MEAP segment. Orders were favorably impacted by $34.3 million from changes in foreign currency exchange rates.

The Company's backlog as of December 31, 2025 was $793.5 million, a 22.0% increase from the December 31, 2024 backlog of $650.2 million. The increase in backlog from December 31, 2024 was primarily attributable to the higher orders as discussed above. Backlog was favorably impacted by $32.4 million from changes in foreign currency exchange rates.

A detailed discussion of the year-over-year changes for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023 can be found in the Management's Discussion and Analysis section of the Company's 2024 Annual Report on Form 10-K filed on February 21, 2025, and is available on the SEC's website at www.sec.gov as well as in the "Investors" section of our website at www.manitowoc.com.

Consolidated net sales for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased 2.9% to $2,240.9 million from $2,178.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2024. The increase was primarily attributable to $50.6 million of higher new tower crane shipments in the EURAF segment, $51.0 million of higher non-new machine sales, and $15.5 million of higher revenue due to price

realization and favorable product mix in the Americas segment. This was partially offset by lower new crane shipments in the Americas segment and European mobiles business. Net sales were favorably impacted by $35.3 million from changes in foreign currency exchange rates.

Gross profit for the year ended December 31, 2025 increased 7.9% to $404.7 million compared to $375.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2024. The increase was primarily attributable to the higher net sales and favorable product mix. This was partially offset by lower absorbed costs due to lower manufacturing volume in the Americas segment and $6.1 million of net tariff costs.

paragraphs: The Manitowoc Company, Inc. ("Manitowoc" or the "Company") 於 1902 年成立，總部設於美國威斯康辛州密爾沃基市。Manitowoc 透過其全資子公司，提供高品質、以客戶為中心的起重產品與服務，遍及全球，透過 Grove、Manitowoc、National Crane、Potain、Shuttlelift 及 Upfits by Aspen Equipment 品牌，以及其以支援為導向的子公司 MGX Equipment Services。如需更多資訊，請造訪 www.manitowoc.com。我們網站上的資訊並非本文件或任何其他我們向美國證券交易委員會 (SEC) 提交或提供的報告的一部分，亦未經引用納入本文件。

本公司有三個應報告分部；美洲分部、歐洲與非洲 ("EURAF") 分部，以及中東與亞太 ("MEAP") 分部。美洲報告分部包括北美洲與南美洲大陸。EURAF 報告分部包括歐洲與非洲大陸，除外中東地區。MEAP 報告分部包括亞洲與澳洲大陸以及中東地區。這些分部係根據 "管理方法" 來識別，此方法指明管理層用以做出營運決策及評估績效的內部組織。如需更多有關我們報告分部的資訊，請參閱第二部分，第 7 項 "管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析" 以及附註 17，"分部"。
Manitowoc 的願景是我們為當前與未來世代建造實體社區與結構。我們的使命與此願景緊密相連；我們渴望在起重產業中提供最高層級的客戶信心與信任。我們的核心價值觀是員工的指導原則，確保我們達成願景與使命。這些核心價值觀為：
(1) 我們的客戶成功時，我們也成功：我們致力於客戶的成功，我們每次皆提供以客戶為先的體驗，我們致力於每日改善客戶體驗，並提供可靠且優秀的服務。
(2) 我們做正確的事：我們以安全且環境責任的方式工作，我們尊重他人，我們以道德的方式行事，並提供優質的成果。
(3) 我們以團隊為中心工作：我們協助彼此達成客戶需求，我們以團隊為先，我們合作並支持團隊成員，並促進開放、雙向的溝通。
(4) 我們交付成果：我們做到我們承諾的事，我們專注於持續改進與創新，並努力超越客戶期望。
(5) 我們以榜樣為導向：我們慶祝成功並從失敗中學習，我們以積極樂觀的態度面對每一天，並享受樂趣。
Manitowoc 正從以產品為導向的公司轉型為以客戶為中心的企業，專注於提供完整的起重服務，以擴大我們的後市場業務。在持續致力於開發創新起重產品及強大新產品開發管道的同時，我們透過 CRANES+50 策略擴大非新機銷售。非新機銷售較少需要資本投入，更具利潤性，且較不具週期性。我們的長期目標是為股東產生可持續的回報，使 Manitowoc 成為更具競爭力且更強韌的公司。

我們於 2021 年啟動 CRANES+50 策略，以專門擴大非新機銷售，將本公司從以產品為導向的業務轉型為以客戶為中心的企業，提供完整的起重服務，以擴大我們的後市場業務。此轉變對我們的長期願景至關重要。CRANES+50 策略遠不僅是後市場的漸進成長；同時也關於為客戶提供完整的起重解決方案。這包括透過擴大分銷範圍來強化我們的服務據點、以新且補充性的產品擴大產品組合、提供更多的服務選項，並導入數位解決方案，為客戶提供優質的附加價值支援。

值得注意的計畫包括以下內容：

美洲：2021年，本公司取得Aspen Equipment Company（"Aspen"）與H&E Equipment Services, Inc.（現為MGX Equipment Services, LLC，或稱"MGX Equipment Services"）的起重機業務資產，擴大了本公司提供新機銷售、二手機銷售、零組件、再製造與服務支援給多種終端市場客戶的能力。2022年，本公司完成取得Honnen Equipment Company（"Honnen"）起重機租賃 fleet 資產，擴大了本公司在科羅拉多州、懷俄明州與內布拉斯加州的租賃 portfolio 與直接對客戶的據點。此外，2023年，本公司新增關鍵區域包括密蘇裏州與南卡羅來納州，2024年，本公司遷移至較大的據點於路易斯安那州與亞利桑那州。2025年初，本公司在田納西州納什維爾擴建了廠區，並取得Ring Power Corporation的某些區域與相關資產，進一步擴大了本公司在喬治亞州、北卡羅來納州與南卡羅來納州的直接對客戶區域。取得這些業務資產與新增區域的資產，促進了本公司在北美地區擴大後市場活動的策略。本公司目前在15個州設有17個全服務據點，擁有超過175名現場服務工程師，提供業界領先的技術專業與優異的客戶支援。2026年初，本公司宣佈與Hiab簽訂新分銷協議，提供載重機於13個州的產品，擴大本公司可銷售給客戶的產品種類，並提供這些產品的服務。

歐洲與中東及亞洲太平洋（EURAF and MEAP）：自2021年起，本公司將歐洲塔式起重機租賃 fleet 的原設備成本增加27.3 百萬美元，以強化對客戶的支援。本公司持續提升在歐洲進行後市場服務的 portfolio，例如零件與整機配件銷售、現場修理、技術支援、組裝與拆卸服務、起重機再製造、培訓服務與數位解決方案。2025年，本公司在法國默爾、法國布瓦耶與波蘭華沙開設新設與升級的服務據點，強化對客戶的服務覆蓋範圍。在歐洲，本公司目前在八個國家設有17個服務據點，擁有超過220名現場服務工程師。此外，本公司在澳洲的據點根據客戶需求，擴大了所提供的服務與補充產品。

概觀：曼迪沃克公司股份有限公司（"Manitowoc" 或 "本公司"）於1902年成立，總部設於美國威斯康辛州密爾瓦基市。本公司透過其全資子公司，透過Grove、Manitowoc、National Crane、Potain、Shuttlelift及Upfits by Aspen Equipment品牌與其支援導向子公司MGX Equipment Services，提供高品質、以客戶為導向的起重產品與服務，業務遍及全球。如需更多資訊，請造訪www.manitowoc.com。本公司網站的資訊並非本申報表或任何其他申報文件的一部分，亦未經引用 herein。
所有金額單位皆為百萬美元，除非另有說明，否則所有表格中包含的金額皆為百萬美元。
訂單與待履行訂單並非美國通用會計原則（"GAAP"）所定義的衡量指標，本公司用以確定訂單與待履行訂單的方法可能與其他公司不同。管理階層使用訂單與待履行訂單進行產能與資源規劃。本公司認為此資訊對投資人而言是有用的，可提供未來營收的指標。待履行訂單代表預期將認列為淨銷售額之訂單之金額。當本公司已收到具有最低價格之執行中契約，但尚未認列為淨銷售額時，該訂單將列入待履行訂單。
2025年12月31日財年訂單金額較2024年同期增加22.7%，由1,922.8百萬美元增至2,359.0百萬美元。訂單增加主要由於美洲與EURAF分部之需求增加。此部分抵銷了MEAP分部需求減少的影響。訂單因外幣交換率變動而有利增加34.3百萬美元。
本公司2025年12月31日之待履行訂單為793.5百萬美元，較2024年12月31日之650.2百萬美元增加22.0%。待履行訂單較2024年12月31日增加主要由於上述訂單增加。待履行訂單因外幣交換率變動而有利增加32.4百萬美元。
2024年12月31日與2023年12月31日之年度變動詳細討論，可於本公司2024年度10-K申報表之管理階層財務狀況與營運成果分析部分找到，該申報表於2025年2月21日提交，並可在SEC網站www.sec.gov取得，同時亦可在本公司網站投資者專區www.manitowoc.com取得。

headings: 與本公司業務、營運及產業相關之風險
總體經濟情勢及國際政治事件可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、現金流及營運成果造成重大不利影響。
由於我們參與之終端市場屬高度競爭，若我們未能有效應對或未能有效回應競爭，本公司之淨銷售額及獲利可能下降。
不公平之國際競爭可能對本公司財務結果造成不利影響。
本公司在美國境外有大量產品製造與銷售，此國際營運可能面臨這些國家特有的多項風險。
若我們未能開發新穎產品，或本公司市場之客戶不接受這些產品，本公司之營運結果可能受到負面影響。
本公司依賴關鍵高階主管、經理及專業人員，並可能面臨難以延攬及留任合格員工之困難。
本公司可能無法維持其工程、技術及製造專業能力。
任何資訊系統的中斷都可能中斷我們的營運，並對我們的業務及財務運作造成不利影響。
若我們未能識別、管理、完成並適當整合併購、戰略聯盟、合作企業或其他重大交易，可能會對我們未來的營運成果造成不利影響。
若我們未能維持有效的產品與服務分銷網路，可能會影響我們的業務及財務結果。
我們在許多營運國家的營運成本持續增加，可能會對我們的業務及財務結果造成不利影響。
若我們遭遇勞資關係問題，可能會影響我們的營運及獲利能力。
我們若無法從天然或人為災難或公共衛生危機中復原，可能會對我們的業務及財務結果造成不利影響。
財務風險
部分客戶可能無法從第三方取得融資以購買我們的產品，我們可能因協助客戶取得第三方融資而產生相關費用。
本公司 leverage 可能影響本公司營運及財務狀況。
本公司營運結果受匯率及其他貨幣風險影響。匯率大幅波動可能對本公司營運結果及現金流產生不利影響。
對額外稅務負擔的暴露可能對本公司營運結果產生負面影響。
本公司 goodwill 及無形資產佔本公司總資產相當大比例；因此，減損費用已對本公司營運結果產生，且未來可能繼續對本公司營運結果產生不利影響。
本公司面臨與退休金及其他退休後福利義務相關的風險。
法律及法規風險
可能產生的環境負債可能屬重大性。
本公司國際銷售及營運受適用於貿易、關稅、出口管制及外國貪腐行為的法律規範影響，違反這些法律規範可能對本公司營運產生不利影響。

paragraphs: 本公司的財務狀況、營運成果及現金流受多種風險影響，許多風險並非完全在本公司控制範圍內，可能導致實際表現與歷史或預期未來表現有重大差異。投資人應謹慎考量本年度報告表10-K所載資訊，並參考下文所述風險因素。
總體經濟情況，包括通貨膨脹、利率偏高及關稅，以及先前供應鏈、勞動力及物流限制，已對我們轉化積壓訂單為營業收入（銷售時間點）產生負面影響，並可能持續產生負面影響，這可能，且已經，影響我們的財務狀況、現金流及營運成果。此外，先前的運輸限制導致某些地區的出貨延遲。持續或惡化的總體經濟情況可能對我們的財務狀況、營運成果及/或現金流產生重大不利影響。
地緣政治事件，包括烏克蘭及中東地區的持續衝突，已導致並可能持續導致物流限制、物流成本上升，以及歐洲地區原材料及零組件成本的重大波動，加劇通貨膨脹及關稅情況，這可能對我們的財務狀況、營運成果及/或現金流產生重大不利影響。
本公司業務受多種風險影響，包括但不限於美國或其他國家所實施的關稅及其他貿易保護措施，以及美國與國際貿易關係，包括與中國及歐盟的關係。
截至2025年12月31日，美國已與關鍵夥伴包括歐盟、日本及英國簽訂國家特定貿易協議，包含修改後的關稅結構及產業特定豁免。的
美國持續與其他國家進行貿易協議談判，包括中國，目前這些國家的相互關稅各有不同。此外，美國政府對新鋼鐵及鋁合金衍生產品課徵50%關稅，這些產品包含本公司部分起重機零組件及型號。這些關稅適用於來自幾乎所有國家的進口，英國則適用較低的25%關稅率。
